_doc: Resource definitions per sim/geography/resources_catalogue.py. mechanism: mineral_deposit | point_occurrence | surface_stock | biotic_stand. unit: the quantity unit; with grade_basis true, contained quantity = ore tonnes x grade in that unit per tonne (key median_<unit>_per_tonne). deposit_types: {id, deposits_per_million_km2 (per million km2 of fully permissive land, before clustering), tonnage_lognormal {median_tonnes, sigma (ln)}, grade_lognormal, depth_class, small_scale, permissive_when [conditions], envelope [suitability entries], layer_weights [{layer, weights, default, if_missing}], provincial_only (only near catalogue deposits of that type), clusters (false: no boost from neighbours), gem_fraction {median, sigma}}. Densities are tile averages, heuristic stand-ins for a geologic-province layer (e.g. Hasterok 2022) that would replace the relief and climate proxies. Giants beyond the truncation of the lognormal come only from the known-deposit catalogue. Gems are point occurrences (pipes, gravels, veins) with gem_fraction of carats of cuttable quality; all gated to known provinces because no geology layer exists.

deposit_types.source: Singer 2008, Cox and Singer 1986 (USGS Bull 1693), Singer and Mosier grade-tonnage models; values from memory, check before relying
